events.text: New Year at {bh_the}, and the seating plan has been written out by {npc} personally. You find your name at the far end of the lower table, between the man who mends the roof and an empty stool kept for a dead dog. {npc} bows when you arrive. "We did so want you to feel at home," {he} says, loud enough to carry.

choices.text: Sit down, and ask after the dog

effects.log: You ask after the dog with real interest. It turns out to have been a good dog. The roof man tells you about it for an hour, and you learn more about the back stairs of this house than a year of bowing would have taught you.

choices.text: Make a toast to the seating, with a straight face

ok.log: You thank {npc} for the place of honour beside the household's most loyal member. The upper table laughs before it can stop itself. {npc} does not.

mem.note: made me a joke at the New Year table

fail.log: It comes out sharper than you meant, and nobody laughs at all. You drink alone, and {npc} makes a small note on the back of the plan.

choices.text: Leave the table, and eat in your rooms

effects.log: You eat cold dumplings at your own desk, and the whole house knows by morning that the guest has feelings.

events.text: {npc} has been told to spar with you "so that the young may learn from our guest." {He} arrives with six cousins to watch and a wooden sword, and offers you the one with the split handle. "Our best visitors' sword," {he} says. "We keep the good ones for family."

choices.text: Take the split sword, and take {him} apart with it

ok.log: It takes four moves. You hand the split sword back to {npc} handle first. Six cousins develop a sudden interest in the far wall, and the training yard is very polite to you for a month.

mem.note: shamed me before the cousins with a broken sword

fail.log: The handle comes apart in your palm at the wrong moment, and {npc} is good. The cousins clap. Your hand heals; the story does not.

choices.text: Lose, slowly, and let {him} enjoy it

effects.log: You lose at a sensible pace and bow at the end. {npc} tells it at dinner as a triumph. You spent the bout learning exactly how the {bh_art} opens, which is more than {he} learned of you.

choices.text: Bow, and say a guest does not cross blades with the blood

effects.log: It is an excellent excuse, and they know it, and they have to accept it. {npc} calls you careful. In this house, that is not meant kindly.

events.text: Your orders came from the head of the house, in writing. {npc} reads them, holds them up to the light, and hands them back. "Forgive me. I do not take instruction from the guest wing. Perhaps you could have someone of the name repeat it to me?" Forty retainers are pretending to count arrows.

choices.text: Go and find someone of the name to repeat it

effects.log: You walk the length of the compound, and you find a nine-year-old cousin, and you bring the child back by the hand to say the words. Nobody laughs, because you do not.

choices.text: Repeat the order, quietly, once

ok.log: You say it again, no louder. Something in how you say it makes {npc} remember an appointment with the arrows. It gets done. You will pay for that look later, and you know it.

mem.note: gave me an order, as if a guest could

fail.log: {npc} smiles and waits, and you are left holding your paper in front of forty men. It gets done two days late, by someone else.

choices.text: Report it to {bh_head}

effects.log: The head of the house hears you out, and sighs, and speaks to {npc}, and nothing changes except that now you are the guest who complains.

mem.note: carried tales to the head of the house

events.text: The tablets of {bh_the} are being cleaned for the spring rites. You offer to help carry them, since you are passing and they are heavy. {npc} takes the first one out of your arms as if you had picked up a baby by one foot. "Those hands have not been presented to the ancestors," {he} says. There is a bucket you may carry instead.

choices.text: Carry the bucket

effects.log: You carry the bucket, all day, past nine hundred years of names. By the end you have read most of them. It is useful to know how many of them died in their own hall.

choices.text: Set the tablet down, and walk away

effects.log: You walk away. Nobody calls you back, and nobody mentions it, and from then on the rites are always somewhere you are not.

choices.text: Name the third tablet from the left, and what that ancestor did to get there

ok.log: That ancestor married in, as it happens, and took the name four hundred years ago. {npc} goes the colour of old paper. It is not a thing anybody says aloud here, and now you have said it.

fail.log: You have the wrong ancestor, and the wrong century. {npc} corrects you kindly, in front of everyone, with dates.

events.text: Your name is missing from the winter rice list again. {npc}, who keeps it, is sure it is a mistake, and is sure it can be mended, and is sure you will understand that the blood must be fed first in a lean year. The storehouses are so full that the mice are getting fat. {He} shows you the list. It is beautifully written.

choices.text: Buy your own rice, and say nothing

effects.log: You send out for rice, and you pay the market price, and you have it carried in past the gate in plain view. It costs you, and it costs them more.

choices.text: Take it up with the steward

effects.log: The steward finds your name in a different ledger, under a different year, and nothing is ever said to {npc}. You eat. It takes eleven visits.

choices.text: Go hungry and train through it

effects.log: You train on broth for one winter. Your body has been hungrier than this, and it hardens a little. Nobody notices, and that was the idea.

events.text: A visiting scholar at dinner asks who you are. {npc} answers for you, warmly. "Oh, that is one of ours. Well. Not one of ours. One of the people who is here." The scholar nods politely and turns back to the people who matter. {npc} refills your cup {him}self, which is somehow the worst part.

choices.text: Thank {him} for the wine

effects.log: You thank {him}. {npc} looks slightly disappointed. It is a small thing, and you keep it.

choices.text: Ask the scholar about the error in chapter nine

ok.log: You and the scholar are still arguing at midnight, and the scholar asks for your name twice, and writes it down. {npc} has gone to bed. A letter comes in the spring addressed to you, by name, at this house.

fail.log: There is no error in chapter nine. The scholar explains why, at length, and with sympathy.

events.text: A marriage was supposed to end this. At the family banquet, {npc} seats you with the servants of the bride's side and calls it an old custom. There is no such custom. You have read the house rules. {He} wrote this one this morning, and the ink on the place card is still soft.

choices.text: Sit with the servants, and be good company

effects.log: You sit. By the third dish the servants of the house have told you who is sleeping where and who owes what. It is the best seat in the hall, as it turns out.

choices.text: Ask the head of the house to read the custom aloud

ok.log: There is a long silence while nobody can find it. A chair is brought for you at the family table, and {npc} has to carry it. Now you have an enemy who knows how to carry a chair.

mem.note: made me carry a chair across the banquet

fail.log: The head of the house says old customs are old customs, and returns to the soup.

events.text: There is a word the young of {bh_the} have for someone who marries in, and {npc} has taught it to the small children, who shout it across the yard with great joy and no idea what it means. A small child tells you, seriously, that it means "friend." The child offers you half a persimmon.

choices.text: Take the persimmon, and answer to the word

effects.log: You take the persimmon, and you answer to it. In a year the children are saying it the way they say "uncle." {npc} has no idea what to do about that.

choices.text: Find {npc}, and tell {him} what you heard

effects.log: {npc} is delighted that you heard. There is nothing you can do to a man who has been waiting all year for you to be angry.

mem.note: finally noticed what the children call them

events.text: The one you married tells you, across the pillow, that the aunts have asked whether the children of this marriage will be entered in the register or kept in the side book. It is said lightly. It was not asked lightly. Tomorrow you are expected at breakfast with those same aunts, and with {npc}, who suggested the side book in the first place.

choices.text: Say the children will be in the register, or the house can do without them

effects.log: You say it to their faces at breakfast. Nobody answers, and someone passes the pickles. The register is not mentioned again, which is not the same as an answer.

choices.text: Find the old rule, and bring it to breakfast

ok.log: Children of a marriage go in the register: it is in the founder's own hand. You leave the page beside the pickles, and {npc} stops suggesting things for a while.

fail.log: The rule you find has been amended, twice, by people with this surname.

events.text: Since your name went on the register, {npc} has taken to calling you "cousin" in every sentence, and then pausing for one breath afterward. "Cousin." The breath. "Will you be joining us?" Everyone can hear the breath. It is an extraordinary piece of work, and {he} has clearly practised.

choices.text: Start pausing after {his} name as well

effects.log: You pick it up in a week. Soon the two of you are holding whole conversations made of pauses, and the juniors have started to take sides, and some of them are on yours.

choices.text: Let it go by

effects.log: You let it go by, every day, for years. It does less than you feared, and more than you would admit.

events.text: The register says you are of {bh_the}. The cook has not read the register. Neither has the old master of the training yard, who sends you back to the guest wing to wash, and {npc}, standing close behind, who would like it known that {he} did not suggest it. Your new robes have the crest on them. It is on slightly crooked. You did not sew it.

choices.text: Unpick the crest, and sew it straight yourself

effects.log: You sit in the yard and do it where people can see. Your stitching is terrible. An old aunt takes the robe off you without a word, fixes it, and hands it back, and that is the first thing anyone of the blood has done for you.

choices.text: Show the old master why they wrote your name down

ok.log: The old master is on the ground for only a moment, and comes up laughing. "That one is ours," the yard is told, and you wash where the family washes. {npc} watches all of it.

mem.note: won over the old master in front of me

fail.log: The old master is very old, and very good, and you wash in the guest wing.

events.text: Spring rites. For the first time, you are allowed to kneel with the family before the tablets. {npc} has knelt directly behind you, and all through the long reading of the names you hear {him}, very softly, counting them. When {he} reaches the end, {he} whispers: "And nobody after. Nobody who was not born to it. Do remember."

choices.text: Stay on your knees until the rite is done

effects.log: You stay. You know the names by now. You know the one four hundred years back who was no more born to it than you. You keep that for a better day.

choices.text: Add your own name aloud at the end of the reading

effects.log: Your voice is clear, and it carries. The priest loses the place. In the whole house, only the very old women are smiling, and they do not explain why.

events.text: You hold the seat of {bh_the}. Today {npc}, of the blood, has refused to sign the grain order, for the third time, on the grounds that the seal on it "does not seem to be the family's, quite." It is the family's. You are holding it. The grain is rotting at the docks while they discuss this.

choices.text: Sign it yourself, and read the name of each refuser into the record

ok.log: The grain moves. The list of names is very short by evening, because nobody wants to be on it. They hate you a little more, and they eat.

fail.log: They let you read the names and they sign nothing. The grain moves on your own silver, and you lose a month.

choices.text: Have someone of the blood sign in your place

effects.log: A nervous cousin signs. The grain moves. You have just agreed, in writing, that your signature is not quite enough. You are aware of it.

events.text: A marriage broker has written to the head of {bh_the} about the heir's match. The letter is addressed, with great courtesy, to {npc}. So is the next one. So is the invitation from the Governor. {npc} brings them to you each morning on a small tray, unopened, with an expression of pure innocence.

choices.text: Answer every letter in your own hand, and sign as head

effects.log: You answer them all. In a few years the letters will come to you. You will always know they did not start out that way.

choices.text: Tell {npc} the tray is a kindness, and make it a post

ok.log: Keeper of the Head's Correspondence. It has a small stipend and a smaller office. {npc} is furious, and {he} cannot refuse without saying why. The letters are on time now.

fail.log: {npc} accepts the post, with a bow, and the letters start going astray.

events.text: The head's chair of {bh_the} was made for someone with longer legs nine generations ago, and your feet do not quite sit right on the footstool. The first time you noticed, you thought nothing of it. Then you saw that {npc} has been standing where {he} can see your feet at every audience, and that {he} is teaching the juniors to look.

choices.text: Have the chair cut down to fit

effects.log: A carpenter takes two inches off nine generations. There is an uproar. You sit comfortably in it, and you will never hear the last of it, and you find that you can live with that.

choices.text: Leave it, and grow into it

effects.log: You leave it alone. You sit very straight. After a few years nobody looks at your feet any more, or you have stopped checking.

events.text: {npc} has insulted you at the gate, in front of the Wudang envoys. It is the usual insult. The difference is that the envoys can feel what you are, and they have gone pale, and are looking at {npc} the way one looks at a child playing with a lit firework. By evening {bh_head} has sent {npc} to you with an apology, a jar of old wine, and a stiff back.

choices.text: Accept the cup, and be gracious

effects.log: You pour {him} a cup yourself. {npc}'s hand shakes a little. Your graciousness costs the house more than any punishment would have, and the head knows it, and thanks you for it through clenched teeth.

mem.note: made me bow, and poured me wine for it

choices.text: Send it back, and ask for the manual {he} has been keeping from you instead

effects.log: The manual arrives that night, wrapped in silk, with nobody's name on it. They need you. It is very clear to everyone now how much.

events.text: The Black Wind has come for the salt road, and the fighting men of {bh_the} are young. {bh_head} comes to your rooms in person, sits down in the chair for visitors, and is silent for some time. {npc} waits at the door, not looking in. "We have not always been kind," says the head of the house. "You will have noticed. Will you ride?"

choices.text: Ride, and name no price

effects.log: You ride. The Black Wind stops being a difficulty on the third day. You name no price, and they will spend years trying to work out what that means.

choices.text: Ride, for first pick of the library

effects.log: You ride. You come back to a library whose door has been left open for you, ahead of people with the name. A cousin is made to wait outside until you finish.

choices.text: Let the young learn

effects.log: You stay in your rooms. Some of the young do learn. Some of them come home on carts. The head of the house does not ask you for anything again, and you notice how quiet it gets.

events.text: A ten-year-old of the blood has walked into your rooms, sat down and announced that everybody says you could beat Grandfather, and could you show how? {npc} arrives out of breath a moment later, and stops in the door when {he} sees you are holding the child's sword hand and adjusting the wrist. Nobody has told you that you are forbidden to. Nobody has ever needed to.

choices.text: Finish the lesson

effects.log: You finish the lesson. It is a good wrist. {npc} stands there the whole time. Whatever is said about it later is said very carefully, because that child keeps coming back, and because of who you are.

choices.text: Send the child off, gently

effects.log: You send the child back to the family wing with a sweet. {npc} bows slightly lower than usual, and you are not sure which of you was just protected.

events.text: The treasury of {bh_the} has offered you a new title, a stipend, and a house by the lake. {npc} delivers the news with a face like a shut door. All the gifts come with the same small condition: you should be seen less, in the main hall, on feast days. They would like to have your strength. They would also like not to have to look at it.

choices.text: Take the house by the lake

effects.log: It is a lovely house. You have a good view of the whole compound from it. They had not thought about that.

choices.text: Take the stipend, and come to every feast

effects.log: You come to every feast. You sit very quietly. You eat a great deal. It is the only thing about you they have never managed to complain about.

events.text: A young master of a friendly house, here for the betrothal talks, has called you "the family's hired dog" in front of the whole hall. Then the young master looks round to see who laughed. Nobody did. {npc}, who has called you worse this week, has gone white. {bh_head} is standing before you have put your cup down, apologizing to you, in public, for a guest of the house.

choices.text: Let the head of the house handle it

effects.log: The young master is on the road by nightfall and the betrothal is off. It costs {bh_the} more than you could have cost them. They paid it, and you did not have to lift a finger.

choices.text: Stand up, and ask the young master for a friendly bout

ok.log: It is friendly for almost a full exchange. The young master leaves in a litter, and the family sends you a gift. No one at that table ever says the word dog again.

fail.log: The young master is better than expected. You win, barely, and it costs you more than the insult did, and everyone saw how close it was.

events.text: Council day at {bh_the}. They are about to send the youngest branch to hold the river forts, because the main line does not want to. You are External. Your seat is by the door, with the draught. You have also held river forts, and they have not. Every elder at the table knows that, and every elder is carefully looking somewhere else.

choices.text: Say what will happen to those children

effects.log: You say it plainly: how long the forts will last, and how it will end. A long silence. The order goes out changed. Half of them will never forgive you for being right where they could hear.

choices.text: Keep your counsel, and send the branch your own supplies

effects.log: You say nothing and you send grain and arrow-shafts downriver under no name. The young ones hold. They find out who sent it. Nobody at the table does.

events.text: The council of {bh_the} is deciding whether to ride out in the sects' quarrel. {bh_head} wants to. The elders of the blood want what {bh_head} wants, and nobody has asked the one at the end of the table, who will be doing most of the actual riding. You clear your throat. It is very quiet in here, all of a sudden.

choices.text: Argue for staying home

effects.log: You argue it well, from the seat by the door. Horses are unsaddled by evening. It may even have been the right thing. They will never say so.

choices.text: Say you will ride where you are sent

effects.log: You say it. A few of them relax. You are useful and you are obedient, and neither of those things is what they are actually afraid of.

events.text: There is a motion before the council of {bh_the} to remove the External seats altogether, moved by a young elder of the blood who needs something to be known for. The others will not support it. They also will not oppose it. They would like to see what you do. You have, in your sleeve, a list of what this young elder owes, and to whom.

choices.text: Read out the list

effects.log: You read it out. You do not raise your voice. The motion dies on the table, and so does a career, and nobody at the council meets your eye for the rest of the year.

choices.text: Second the motion, and ask who will hold the north gate without you

ok.log: There is a very long pause while they work out who would hold it. The young elder withdraws the motion with a graceful speech, and you all pretend it was his idea.

fail.log: They think about it, and they think someone could. It only fails by one vote.

events.text: {bh_head} sends for you and offers tea in the small room, the one for family. "You have done much for us. It seems wrong that you should grow old in the guest wing." There is a niece, a grown one, or a nephew if you would rather, of good character and low rank in the name. Everything is ready. The room has no other door. It is the kindest trap you have ever been offered.

choices.text: Accept

effects.log: They are very happy for you. You look at the person they chose, who looks back at you with the same clear understanding, and you both bow. You are of the house now, by marriage, and watched at home too.

choices.text: Thank them, and refuse

effects.log: You find the words. They are very gracious words. The tea is cold by the end of them. Now {bh_head} knows you would rather stay outside and be feared, and will act on it.

events.text: The matchmaker of {bh_the} has been to your rooms three times this year, each time to say she has merely been passing. Today she has brought a painted scroll of someone of the name, of grown years, and a letter from {bh_heir} which says how pleased everyone would be. The scroll is flattering. The letter is an order that has learned good manners.

choices.text: Say yes before they ask a fourth time

effects.log: You say yes. The wedding is enormous, and the guest list is a map of everyone who now has a reason to keep an eye on you. Your name goes in the side book first, and then the main one.

choices.text: Keep her coming, year on year, with fine excuses

ok.log: She comes back with a new scroll every spring for a long time, and she enjoys it. Each visit buys you another year, and they feel they are making progress.

fail.log: She looks at your fine excuse, and rolls up her scroll, and goes straight to {bh_head} without stopping for tea.

events.text: A letter on heavy paper. In recognition of long service, you are to be styled Honoured Pillar of {bh_the}, with a stipend, and rooms nearer the main hall, and a seat one place further from the door. It is a real promotion. You note that the new rooms face the steward's window, and that the stipend must be collected in person.

choices.text: Accept the honour

effects.log: You move your things. The rooms are warmer. The steward waves from his window every morning. You have rarely been so comfortable, or so easy to find.

choices.text: Decline, with deep humility

effects.log: You write back that you are unworthy. Nobody has ever said that to them and meant it, and nobody thinks you do either. {bh_head} folds the letter very small.

events.text: {bh_heir} comes to the guest wing in person, and sits on your step like an old friend. They want you to take on the training of the young of the name. An honour, unheard of for someone from outside. You would have the run of the yard and the respect of a whole generation, and you would also have no time at all for anything else. {bh_heir} smiles, and it is quite a good smile.

choices.text: Take the post

effects.log: You take it. The children are good. You like them more than you expected, and the house has noticed, and that was also the idea.

choices.text: Take the post, and start teaching them what they are not supposed to know

ok.log: A generation of the blood grows up thinking well of you and thinking for itself. It takes them years to see what you have done. It is the slowest knife in the house.

fail.log: A cousin of eleven repeats a lesson at dinner. The post is thanked out of your hands within the month.

events.text: At the head of the ancestral hall of {bh_the} there is a stone that everyone who holds a post of trust has laid a palm on. Nobody has asked this of a guest in living memory, and now {bh_head} is asking, kindly, with the elders in their good robes. "Only the old words. That you will not lift a hand against the house. It would put so many people's minds at rest."

choices.text: Lay your palm on the stone

effects.log: The stone is cold and the words are short. They all smile. It would not stop you, if you chose. But it is said that an oath at that stone stays with you, and you can feel that it has.

choices.text: Offer a different oath, in your own words

ok.log: You swear never to lift a hand against the house while the house keeps faith with you. It sounds so much like what they wanted that it takes the old lawyer a whole day to find the hole, and by then it is carved.

fail.log: They hear the hole at once. There is a silence in which every elder updates their opinion of you.

choices.text: Refuse

effects.log: You say that a guest's word has always been enough here, and you bow, and you leave. By evening the whole compound knows that the guest would not touch the stone.

events.text: An old custom has been remembered. Guests of {bh_the} who hold a seat at the council are asked to leave something in the family's keeping, as a surety of good faith: a child, in the old days, but they are very modern here. Your blade will do. Or your own art written out in full, for the library. {bh_head} says it is just a formality, and looks tired, and means every word of it.

choices.text: Write out your art for the library

effects.log: You write it out, honestly, all of it. A cousin is reading it by morning. Something that was only yours belongs to them as well now, and they sleep better, and you do not.

choices.text: Refuse, and let them make something of it

effects.log: They make something of it. You always thought they would. But your art is still your own.

events.text: The elders of {bh_the} have made a new post for you: Warden of the Outer Halls, with a stipend, a hall of your own and an authority nobody can quite define. It is on the far side of the mountain. It would be an honour to have someone so capable looking after things so far away. {bh_head} tells you so warmly, and does not walk you to the door.

choices.text: Take the Outer Halls

effects.log: It is a good hall. The young who are sent out there are the ones nobody wants, and you are surprised how much you like them. The council sleeps better with you over the ridge.

choices.text: Stay where you are

effects.log: You thank them and you stay in the main hall, where you can be seen. They had hoped you would go. Now they know you know why.

events.text: A very senior elder of {bh_the}, who has never once spoken to you, stops you in the covered walk and says that it is time the sect thought about the next generation of its council. Your name has come up. A word from {bh_head} could do so much. Naturally there are people who would need reassuring first: there is a list of them, and things you might stop doing.

choices.text: Take the list, and stop doing those things

effects.log: You stop. The name goes forward. You are a little higher, and a little quieter, and you look over the list sometimes in the evening to remember what you gave up.

choices.text: Go on as you were

effects.log: You bow and you go on as you were. The senior elder does not stop you in the covered walk again. He has not stopped anyone twice in sixty years.

events.text: The founder's sword hangs in the great hall of {bh_the}, and the senior ranks are to renew their vows before it this year. It has not been done in a century. It is being done now, and it seems that you are the third name on the list, after two who were clearly added for cover. "To obey the seat, and never contest it." {bh_head} is watching you read it.

choices.text: Say the words

effects.log: You say them before the sword, along with everyone else. The two who were added for cover look relieved. So does the head of the sect, and it is the first time you have seen it.

choices.text: Be away from the mountain that week

effects.log: A very urgent errand comes up. Everyone admires how urgent it is. Your name stays on the list, with nothing beside it, where it can be looked at.

events.text: The sect's law master of {bh_the} has noticed that senior disciples have, by ancient rule, the duty to report all private talk with other seniors to the seat. It has not been enforced since the old wars. He proposes to enforce it, starting with one person, as a test, and he mentions it to you personally, with his eyes on your sleeve.

choices.text: Report in, once a month, with nothing in it

effects.log: Once a month you sit down with the law master and tell him about the weather, thoroughly. It is the most boring hour either of you has ever spent. It makes them feel safer, somehow.

choices.text: Ask for the rule to apply to all seniors, starting with his friends

ok.log: The rule goes quietly back to sleep within the week. Everyone agrees it was a very old rule. The law master bows to you in the walk now, slightly, the way one bows to a dog that has growled.

fail.log: He thinks that is an excellent idea, and he starts with you anyway, and his friends get a warning.

events.text: A gift from the seat of {bh_the}: a black robe with one more silver thread than anyone of your rank has ever worn, and a hall of your own with sixty followers. In the Cult, a gift from above is a leash with a tassel on it, and everybody knows that. Sixty followers means sixty pairs of eyes, and you are not sure yet who they report to.

choices.text: Wear the robe

effects.log: You wear it. You keep sixty followers fed and busy. You learn in a month which eleven of them write letters, and you make sure the letters are dull.

choices.text: Return it, saying you have not earned it yet

effects.log: It comes back to the hall with your thanks. In the Cult nobody has ever returned anything. They talk of nothing else for a season, and not one of them thinks you are modest.

events.text: {bh_head} has summoned you to share a meal on the high terrace, alone. It is a great honour, and very few people have come back down from it the same. Over the third dish you are told that you will take the Southern Command, far from here, with all the fighting and all the glory you could want. The food is excellent. You have been watching what the servants eat first.

choices.text: Take the Southern Command

effects.log: You go south and you fight. It is everything you were promised. Word reaches you, sometimes, of how quiet it has become at the top of the mountain without you.

choices.text: Ask to stay, in a way that flatters

ok.log: You say you could never serve that seat from so far away. It is such shameless flattery that the head of the Cult laughs out loud, and lets you stay, and has your wine tasted thereafter, with an air of concern.

fail.log: The dish you are served next is not the same as the one before. You get down the mountain, and you are ill for a month.

events.text: They bring a cup to your rooms at night, four of the seat's own guard, very polite. Every senior of {bh_the} has drunk from it, they say: a small worm that sleeps quietly, and gives no trouble at all, so long as the antidote comes each year. It is a long tradition. The guard captain looks a bit embarrassed. He has drunk from it too. He does not mind holding the cup for you.

choices.text: Palm the worm, and only pretend to swallow

ok.log: Your hands are quicker than the captain's eyes. The worm goes up your sleeve and into the night soil. Each year, you take the antidote with every sign of gratitude. It tastes dreadful.

fail.log: They see it. The captain sighs, and the other three take your arms. This time they watch you swallow.

choices.text: Lift the cup, in front of them

effects.log: You lift it, and hold it there in front of them all, and set it down. Nobody stops you. It smells of nothing. A very senior elder nods to you the next morning, in a friendly way, for the first time. You now know how friendship is done here.

choices.text: Knock the cup out of his hand

effects.log: It smashes on the stones. The four of them look at the mess, and then at you, and they leave without a word. By morning every lamp in the upper halls is burning later than usual.

events.text: A rite is called at the black altar of {bh_the}. Every senior will cut a palm, and let it fall into the great bowl with the rest, and speak their loyalty to the seat before the whole Cult. {bh_head} will watch each face. It has been held four times in the Cult's history, and each time a few people did not leave the hall.

choices.text: Cut deep, and speak well

effects.log: You give them a good clean cut and a clear voice. The bowl takes it. The next person in line gets it a bit wrong, and you do not look round.

choices.text: Fall ill that week, in a convincing way

ok.log: You are carried to the sick hall with a fever that frightens the physicians. By the time you can stand, the rite is over, and three seniors are missing. You send your regrets.

fail.log: A physician of the seat looks in your mouth, and then at you. He writes something down. You make a remarkable recovery by the following morning.

events.text: The new maid who has been sent to do your rooms folds your letters back along exactly the same creases. It is very good work. It takes a long time to notice, and it took you three years to learn to notice things like that. The maid's cousin works for {npc}. Everyone in this house has a cousin. The maid has just asked if you would like the window shut.

choices.text: Keep the maid, and write letters to be read

effects.log: You start writing very dull letters, and one or two that are not dull at all but are not true. It keeps three people at {bh_the} busy for a year.

choices.text: Send the maid back with a note for {npc}

effects.log: The maid goes back with a polite note on a tray. {npc} now knows you know. That was a pleasure, and it may have been a mistake.

mem.note: sent my girl back with a note

events.text: You come back from the river and everything in your rooms is one finger to the left. All of it. The inkstone, the sword rack, the bed. Nothing has been taken. It takes an entire afternoon for people to move everything one finger to the left and move nothing else. This is {npc}, letting you know how long they had.

choices.text: Move it all back, and say nothing

effects.log: You move it back. It takes you about an hour. The next day, you nod to {npc} in the corridor, and {he} nods back, and neither of you has ever been so polite.

choices.text: Move everything in {his} rooms a finger to the right

ok.log: It takes you three nights. {npc} looks unwell at breakfast for a week. Nobody has ever got into those rooms, and now everyone knows that somebody can.

fail.log: A dog barks at the wrong moment. You are seen, on a roof, at night, near the family wing. There is no good way to explain that.

events.text: A chest of the family's silver has been found under the floor of the guest wing, and {npc} found it, with several witnesses, on the first try. There is a small and tasteful search of your rooms under way. {bh_head} looks grieved. There is a ledger too, in a hand a good deal like yours, and it has already been shown to the elders.

choices.text: Pick the ledger apart in front of them

ok.log: The ink is from a batch sold last spring and the entries go back ten years. You point this out, slowly, and you watch {npc} calculate how much of this {he} can still survive.

mem.note: took my good ledger apart in front of them

fail.log: The ledger holds. Nothing is proved, and nothing needs to be. Your stipend is frozen, your name is whispered, and {npc} is sympathetic.

choices.text: Pay it back, every tael, and say nothing about who put it there

effects.log: You pay what you never took, and you bow. They are a little ashamed. A few of them know. You have made them owe you, and you have also agreed that you are a thief.

choices.text: Say it is all a lie, and let them hear what you think of them

effects.log: You tell the whole hall. It feels wonderful for about as long as it takes to say. They already knew what you think of them, and now they have it in front of witnesses.

events.text: Word has come from the Martial Alliance. It has been told, by nobody in particular, that a certain External Elder of {bh_the} was seen meeting men of the demonic path at Red Crane Ferry. You have never been to Red Crane Ferry. Three people who are very sure you have are staying at an inn at {npc}'s expense, and they have started to remember what you wore.

choices.text: Find the three witnesses, and buy them a better story

ok.log: Two of them remember being elsewhere. The third was never very sure about the robe. The Alliance's letter is filed under nothing. It cost you some sleep, and a good deal of silver you had not planned on.

fail.log: They are honest men, in a way. They are also frightened of someone else. Your visit goes into the file as well.

choices.text: Go to the Alliance yourself and answer it

effects.log: You go, and you stand there, and you answer all their questions in full. Nothing comes of it, except that you have been seen standing there. It costs you a season and some of your name.

events.text: It is held in the main hall, with the doors open so that the retainers can see. {bh_head} reads it out in a tired voice: the charges, the service you have given, the decision of the elders. {bh_The} no longer requires your attendance. Your things have been packed for you, rather well. There are guards on the stairs, but not enough of them. They did not want a fight. They wanted you to walk.

choices.text: Walk

effects.log: You walk the length of the hall, and you bow to the tablets on your way out, because they cannot stop you doing that. The gate shuts behind you. Whatever you were to this house, you are not that any more.

choices.text: Demand to answer the charges before the whole house

ok.log: You speak for an hour. You name what you did for them, year by year, with the names of the people who are alive because of it. Half the retainers are on their feet by the end. The decision is "deferred." The hall empties very slowly.

fail.log: You speak for an hour. They are polite about it. Then the guards step forward, and you walk anyway, with less than you came in with.

events.text: The tea is the right colour and the right heat, and it smells very faintly of bitter almonds and nothing else, and you have been in {bh_the} long enough to know that the cook never burns her almonds. The boy who brought it is looking at his feet. He is about twelve. Someone told him it was a joke, or told him something worse.

choices.text: Drink nothing, and ask the boy who sent him

ok.log: He cries. He tells you. You give him silver and you send him to a farm you know of by the night road, and you pour the cup out on the roses, which die by morning. Now you have a name.

fail.log: He runs before you can finish the question. The next morning nobody can tell you what boy you mean. The cook has never had a boy.

choices.text: Carry the cup to the main hall, and set it before {bh_head}

effects.log: You set it down in the middle of the morning audience and say that this was sent to you, and that you thought it must be meant for someone else. Nobody picks it up. It sits there all day. It is the most frightened you have ever seen this family.

events.text: You are on the mountain road below the east shrine, on an errand {bh_head} was particularly keen that you run in person, and it is a nice day, and the birds have stopped. There are four on the slope and two behind you, and they fight like nobody in particular. Their swords have had the family marks filed off, and it was done recently, and done by someone who did not expect you to live to look.

choices.text: Kill the ambush where it stands

ok.log: It does not take as long as they were told it would. You keep a sword with a filed hilt. You walk back in at dinner, and you sit down, and you set it beside your bowl, and nobody asks for the salt.

fail.log: You get through them, with a wound that will trouble you for years, and you lie in a ditch until dark. You are not sure which you hate more: them, or how well this was planned.

choices.text: Take the cliff path, and be elsewhere

effects.log: You go off the edge of the road at a run. Thorn scrub takes most of your skin. You do not run the errand. Nobody ever asks you why it was not done.

events.text: You have been at the edge of your next realm for a year, and everyone in {bh_the} knows it, because they know how long you stay in your rooms. A person who is breaking through cannot be interrupted, and everyone knows that too. So why has the inner door been unbarred from the outside, and why is the incense in your room a little sweeter than the one you bought?

choices.text: Stop, put out the incense, and go through the door yourself

ok.log: You lose a year of careful work in one breath, and your arms shake. In the corridor there are two people in soft shoes who were not expecting the door to open. You thank them for coming.

fail.log: You catch it a little late. The sweetness is already in your channels, and it takes you a season to cough it out.

choices.text: Leave the house, and do this in a cave

effects.log: You walk out of the gate at midnight, and you do not tell anyone where you are going. It is a very cold cave. It is a good deal safer than where you live.

events.text: An old physician of {bh_the} comes to your rooms unasked. You are close, he says; he can see that from the door. He has brought a pill. His master, the head of the house, wants you to have it, as a mark of how much your rise will mean to everyone. His hand is not quite steady. He has been in this family for sixty years, and he will not look you in the eye, and he has put it down rather carefully out of his own reach.

choices.text: Thank him, and ask him what he would do

effects.log: He is silent for some time. "I am very old," he says, "and I would not take any medicine I had not made myself." He bows lower than he needs to, and goes. You crush the pill in the yard. Ants will not touch it.

choices.text: Take it apart at the table, grain by grain

ok.log: It is a beautiful piece of work. It would have felt like triumph, right up to the moment your channels opened in the wrong order. You keep what is left. You now know something about the alchemists here.

fail.log: You cannot find anything wrong with it. That frightens you more than anything else this year, and you burn it anyway.

events.text: Your two most promising juniors have been asked to write a short weekly account of your teaching, for the archive of {bh_the}. {npc} proposed it, because the archive is thin on your era. The juniors are mortified. One of them has shown you the first report, with your name spelled wrong, and is about to cry.

choices.text: Help with the spelling, and give them something to write

effects.log: You give them both something to write. It is all true and it is all dull. {npc} reads two years of it with growing suspicion and diminishing hope.

choices.text: Tell them to stop, and take it up in council

effects.log: They stop. You speak to the council, and the council agrees it was all a misunderstanding, and notes that you have sharp ears and loud opinions.

mem.note: took my archive to the council

events.text: A manual is missing from the forbidden shelf of {bh_the}, and {npc} is sure nobody suspects you. {He} has told the library master so at length. It has now been found, as these things are, in the bottom of your clothes chest, by a junior who is very sorry. Your own students are watching from the walk, with their faces carefully arranged.

choices.text: Ask to see the dust on the shelf and on the chest

ok.log: The chest was moved after the manual went in. So was the shelf dust. The library master looks at the marks, and then at {npc}, for a long moment. Nothing is said. You get a very formal apology.

mem.note: looked at the dust

fail.log: There is nothing in the dust. You serve the penalty in silence, and your students stop arranging their faces.

choices.text: Take the punishment, and copy the sutra

effects.log: A year of copying the sect's rule by lamp. You lose some merit and some rank in everyone's eyes. It is very peaceful. You write down the name of everyone who looks at you.

events.text: The council of {bh_the} has met without you, and there is a proposal on the table in the great hall, in your absence, to strike your name for conduct unbecoming: nine charges and a witness to each. {bh_head} sends for you. It is your right to be told before it is done. It is also the last courtesy you are going to get here.

choices.text: Hand in your token, and go

effects.log: You lay the token on the table. It makes a very small sound. The mountain road is long, and it is as beautiful as it was on the day you came.

choices.text: Answer all nine, one at a time

ok.log: It takes until dark. You have your own witnesses, it turns out, and many of them are very young and very stubborn. The council postpones. It has never postponed anything before.

fail.log: You answer all nine, and you answer them well. It was decided before you came up the stairs.

events.text: The rope bridge to the meditation peak of {bh_the} has held for two hundred years. It has been inspected twice this month, and {bh_head} has made a point of telling you so. You are halfway over, on the morning you always cross, when you hear it, a very small tearing sound behind you, like someone biting thread.

choices.text: Run the rope itself as it falls

ok.log: The planks go first. You reach the far side on a rope that is no longer attached to anything. You stand there on the peak, with a long time to think, until they find a way to send someone across for you.

fail.log: You catch the cliff by your fingers, and that is about all you catch. It is a long climb, and you will not ever again use the left wrist the way you did.

choices.text: Throw yourself back the way you came

effects.log: You make it. There is no one on the near side of the bridge, and no one has been there. There is a knife cut in the rope, very neat, the height of a tall person kneeling.

events.text: Your breakthrough is coming, and the elders of {bh_the} have most kindly offered you the Quiet Cell for it, the one with the old array, that only three people have ever been granted. You went to look at it. The array has been repainted. Three of its lines run backward now, in a very steady hand, and they would hold anything in that room quite still.

choices.text: Decline, and do it somewhere else

effects.log: You thank them and you decline. Nobody asks you why. An old array master happens to pass you in the walk, and nods at you, and walks on.

choices.text: Accept, and repaint it yourself the night before

ok.log: You sit down in it the next morning and they close the door, and it holds nothing still at all. When you walk out, stronger, the array master is standing outside. He bows, and you can see him thinking very quickly.

fail.log: You could not read it all. You get out in the fifth hour, with your hands bleeding from the door, and without what you came for.

events.text: {npc} has given you a gift: a quiet young servant to carry your lamp, who cannot hear, or so they tell you. On the third night, you drop a tray behind this servant and the head turns. You both know you saw it. In {bh_the}, that was the moment a servant became a problem, and the servant has gone very pale.

choices.text: Offer a choice, and something to say to {npc}

effects.log: You pull up a stool, ask what the pay is, and double it. In the Cult, it is not the price that makes a spy, but the second price. The lamp goes on being carried.

choices.text: Send the servant back to {npc} alive, with the tray

effects.log: The servant walks back to {npc} carrying a tray with your compliments on it. Nobody in the upper halls has seen such restraint in years. They do not know what to make of it, and they do not like that.

mem.note: sent back my lamp-boy alive, to mock me

events.text: They have found a letter from an orthodox sect in your robes: a warm one, friendly, thanking you for your help. {npc} brought it to the high terrace in person. In {bh_the} this is a very old trick, and everyone knows it is an old trick, and that makes no difference at all. The only question that matters now is whether anyone on the terrace wants it to be true.

choices.text: Make {npc} the more useful one to doubt

ok.log: You say nothing about the letter. You say a lot about the three other letters {npc} carries, which you happen to know about. In an hour the terrace has found a more interesting subject.

fail.log: They find you quite amusing. You lose your command, and your followers are divided up among the people who are still smiling.

choices.text: Offer to take the head of whoever you are accused of helping

effects.log: You ride out in a week with thirty men. When you get back with the proof, the matter of the letter has been forgotten, as these things are, and there is a new tally against your soul.

events.text: The Cult does not expel people. Everyone in {bh_the} knows that. It has made an exception for you, however, because you are too strong to be killed cheaply. A bronze plate with your name on it has been broken on the steps at dawn, in front of the assembled halls. Anyone who speaks to you after sundown will be seen to have spoken to you. It is nearly sundown.

choices.text: Go down the mountain before dark

effects.log: You go. No one stops you. Behind you, in the upper halls, the first lamps are coming on. You have never been so glad to be underestimated, or so sure that you will be sent for.

choices.text: Go up the steps, and sit down on the broken plate

ok.log: You sit there until sunrise. Nobody comes. On the second day, someone brings you tea. On the third, a very senior elder comes, and you discuss what your bronze plate cost, and a new one is made.

fail.log: They do come, as it turns out. You leave in the small hours by a way nobody uses, with a great deal less skin and nothing else.

events.text: It is the bath, in the end. It is always something foolish. There is a scorpion the colour of the bath stone sitting exactly where you put your hand on the rim, on exactly the side you always use, in {bh_the}, where nobody has ever noticed what you do with your hands. You stop with your fingers a thumb-width above it. It does not move. It has been told not to.

choices.text: Kill it, and leave it on the head of the hall's pillow

effects.log: It is a very small body to send such a large message. The head of the hall does not sleep well after that, and says so to nobody.

choices.text: Keep it alive, and find out who has been feeding it

ok.log: It was raised on a very particular herb. Only one garden in the upper halls grows it. You send the keeper of that garden a note saying how much you admire the work.

fail.log: It stings you while you try. You are in bed for a month, and everyone is so sorry to hear it.

events.text: A person on the edge of a realm cannot run. So the Cult has a saying: wait until they close their eyes. You have closed yours, in the deep cell under {bh_the}, and you can hear someone in the passage who is breathing very slowly on purpose. They have been out there for two days. They are very good, and you are nearly through.

choices.text: Finish it, and meet them on the other side

ok.log: The realm opens, and you open your eyes, and the door opens. You look at each other for a moment. They put their knife away, and they bow, because that is what one does, and they go and tell their master how it went.

fail.log: You break off too late and too badly, and your breath tears on the way back. They leave at that sound, satisfied. You will need a very long time to get to this place again.

choices.text: Break off, and take them first

effects.log: You let go of a year of work, and you go through the door. They were not ready for that. Nobody is, and nobody would ever do it, and that was the plan. You sit down again with your hands empty.

events.text: {npc} has sat at the upper table of {bh_the} for fifty years and has refused to learn your name for ten of them. But you have noticed how the old back goes stiff when the talk turns to the heir, and how {he} sits alone at the river every ninth day, at a grave the family does not talk about. Today you have brought a second stool.

choices.text: Sit down, and ask who is buried there

ok.log: A long silence, and then a name, and then an hour. A daughter, thirty years ago, sent on an errand the house needed done. {npc} still does not use your name. {He} says, as you get up, "They would throw you to the same dogs. Come back on the ninth."

fail.log: "Who sent you?" says {npc}, without turning round. Nobody did. It takes you the whole walk home to believe {he} will never believe that.

choices.text: Leave the stool, and go

effects.log: You leave the stool beside the grave and go. It is still there on the next ninth day. So is {npc}. {He} does not look up, but it has been moved a little closer.

mem.note: left a stool at the grave, and asked for nothing

events.text: {npc} is the last person alive who remembers how {bh_the} used to be. {He} thinks the present head is a fool, and {he} has said so at every council for ten years, and nobody listens now because everyone has heard it. You have read every one of the old war-records. You have some questions. Nobody has asked {him} a question in a very long time.

choices.text: Ask, and listen, and come back

ok.log: It takes two winters of tea. {npc} corrects your history at the top of {his} voice, happily, for hours. At the end of the second winter {he} looks at you very sharply. "So," {he} says. "When are you going to do it? I would like to live to see that."

fail.log: {npc} tells you the same story four times, and you can see {he} enjoys it, and you can see that it means nothing. Then a nephew hears of your visits, and they stop.

choices.text: Offer {him} the head's seat at your table, if it ever comes

ok.log: It is a bold thing to say, and {he} laughs until {he} has to be thumped on the back. Then {he} stops laughing. "Yes," says {npc}. "Yes, I expect I would be good at that." You are not certain you have won {him}. You are certain {he} thinks {he} has won you.

fail.log: You get as far as "if it ever comes." {npc} has eyes like an old hawk. "Get out," {he} says, not unkindly, and tells nobody, this time.

events.text: {npc} is young, of the blood, third son of a third son, and better than everyone above {him}, and everyone knows that. {He} has been passed over for the second time this spring. You find {him} hitting a post in the rear yard at midnight. There is blood on the post. You pick up the other practice sword, and you do not say anything.

choices.text: Teach {him} the thing that was wrong with that last turn

ok.log: You work until the sky goes grey, and neither of you says a word about the head of the house. By the end of the month {he} is calling you Teacher when nobody can hear. It is a dangerous thing to be called, and you let {him}.

fail.log: You correct {his} wrist and {he} throws the sword down. "Everyone wants to help," {npc} says, "and they all have the same smile." {He} is not altogether wrong.

choices.text: Tell {him} what you would do in {his} place

ok.log: You lay it out in plain words. {npc} looks at you for a long time and says nothing, but {he} comes to find you the next night. You like how fast {he} learns. It should worry you more that {he} learned that fast.

fail.log: {npc} goes very still. "Is that what you came to say?" {He} walks away, and in a week {he} has been given a post. You wonder how much {he} paid for it.

events.text: There is a duel in the family's yard next week, for a place in the heir's guard. {npc} is going to lose it, because the other one is the head's nephew, and because the judges have been told. {He} knows that. {He} has come to your rooms and is standing in the door, very stiffly, not asking you for anything, with a face that has been up all night.

choices.text: Have a word with one of the judges

effects.log: You have a word. It is short. The nephew loses on points, and no one can quite say how. {npc} takes the post, and {he} says nothing to you afterward, but you can see {him} remembering it.

choices.text: Show {him} what the nephew's left foot gives away

ok.log: {He} wins it clean, in front of everyone, in eleven moves. {He} looks across the yard at you, just once, in the moment when everyone is shouting. That is the thing that you actually came for.

fail.log: {He} tries it too early, and the nephew has been warned about the foot. Somebody in this house is listening at your door.

events.text: {npc} holds all the keys of {bh_the}, and not one of the people who sit at the upper table has ever asked {him} a single question about anything except dinner. {He} also knows to the bushel what the family has been hiding from the tax office, and which cousin has a second household, and what the head of the house really owes. You have come about a leak in your roof. You stay for an hour.

choices.text: Ask about the roof, and notice what {he} is proud of

ok.log: It turns out to be the drains. Nobody has ever noticed the drains. You ask about them in real detail, and at the end of the hour, you are shown a very small account book that nobody else has ever seen. "In case the roof should get worse," says {npc}.

fail.log: {npc} fixes your roof with great courtesy and tells you all about it. {He} also reports your visit in the household log, as {he} does with all of them.

choices.text: Offer {him} silver

effects.log: {npc} looks at the silver. You cannot read that face. "You are very kind," {he} says, and {he} takes it, and bows. You have just learned what {npc} wants you to think {he} costs.

events.text: A bad year: the grain ledger of {bh_the} is short, and {npc} has been told to find the shortage or else be blamed for it. The money went to a cousin's fine new horses. Everyone knows that, and {npc} has no way to say so. You have some grain, and you have noticed, and you have just walked into the counting room with your sleeves rolled up.

choices.text: Quietly make up the shortfall

effects.log: The ledger balances by the end of the week. {npc} watches you sign nothing. You have never seen anyone be so careful to say so little. A month later you begin to get very early notice of things.

choices.text: Find the horses in the ledger, and show {him} how to write it

ok.log: Together you turn the horses into "repairs to the eastern gate." It holds. {npc} takes the pen back very slowly. "You did that very quickly," {he} says. "I will remember how quickly."

fail.log: You cannot make it add up. Neither can {npc}. {He} takes the blame, in the end, and you lose the one person in this house who was in a position to help you.

events.text: {npc} should have been the head of this house. Everyone says so, when they have had enough to drink. {He} was the eldest, the strongest and the best liked, and there was some small matter with {his} mother, and it all went to someone else thirty years ago. {He} is kind to you, and {he} is kind to everyone. You have never once seen {him} sit down with {his} back to a door.

choices.text: Ask {him} to teach you to play stones, and lose honestly

ok.log: After some years {he} says, setting down a stone: "You are not as bad at this as you look, are you." You say nothing. {He} takes three of yours. "Good," says {npc}. "Neither am I. Same time next week."

fail.log: After a year of evenings, {he} puts the board away, and {he} thanks you, and tells you very gently that {he} has heard all of this before.

choices.text: Say to {his} face what everyone says when drunk

effects.log: You say it, sober, across the table. {He} goes on smiling for some time. Then {he} gets up and closes the door. You do not learn until much later whether that was {him} joining you, or {him} deciding how to use you.

events.text: {npc} was married off to the northern branch at nineteen, so that a cousin could have what was promised to {him}. {He} came home widowed, with no rank, and {bh_the} gave {him} a small room and the job of looking after the old people. That was forty years ago. {He} has outlived all of them. {He} knows who said what on each of their deathbeds, and nobody has ever thought to wonder about that.

choices.text: Help {him} carry the water, without being asked

ok.log: You carry water for most of a year. One morning, on the path, {he} says without looking at you: "Your room is watched from the second window, not the first. Go round by the pigs." After that, you always go round by the pigs.

fail.log: {He} lets you carry water for a year, and thanks you each morning. {He} tells you nothing whatever. You are not sure {he} even knows what you wanted.

choices.text: Leave it, and let {him} be

effects.log: You nod to {him} on the path, and leave it. Of everyone in this house, {he} has been used enough. Something in how {he} looks after you makes you think that you may have been noticed for it.

mem.note: left me be, when it would have been useful not to

events.text: There is a persimmon on your windowsill with a thumbnail mark in its skin, which is the sign you agreed on with {npc}, years ago, as a joke. You had thought {he} forgot. You split it open: it says nothing, of course, it is a persimmon. But {he} never does this unless the whole upper table has met without a clerk. You have until about the end of the week.

choices.text: Be elsewhere by the end of the week

effects.log: You find a reason to ride to the far estates. Three days later a good many people visit your rooms, and they find them tidy. They send you their regards. You send them persimmons.

choices.text: Stay, and be very visibly at dinner

effects.log: You go to dinner every night. You ask for second helpings. Whatever they planned, they had planned to do it to someone who did not know. It gets put off, for now.

events.text: {npc} walks past you in the long gallery, in front of two others, and says very loudly that you are an arrogant fool with no manners, and that the head of the house is going to hear about your conduct on the east road. You have not been on the east road. You stop on the next landing. It has been a long time since anyone has been that careful on your behalf.

choices.text: Stay off the east road

effects.log: You stay off the east road. So, you hear, do four men in plain clothes who have been camped beside it for some days, and who go home in the end, grumbling about the price.

mem.note: listened

choices.text: Go down the east road, and take a look at them

ok.log: You meet them at the third milestone. You are very polite. Whoever pays them gets all four swords back, in a neat bundle. You owe {npc} a good deal now, and {npc} has never been so frightened of you.

fail.log: There are more than four. {npc} had not known that, and it is the only thing {he} did not know. You get home, not in good condition.

events.text: A note has been folded into your laundry, in a hand you know: {npc} never did learn to write small. "They know about one of us. They do not know which. They are going to offer each of us something and watch who takes it." It is signed with a small drawing of a pig. You hear someone coming down the corridor, carrying something on a tray.

choices.text: Refuse whatever is on the tray

effects.log: It is a very fine offer. You refuse it with every sign of regret. Later on you see {npc} refusing something too. Neither of you looks up, and you have never trusted anyone so much.

mem.note: understood the note

choices.text: Take it, and make them look at you, not {him}

effects.log: You take it, gladly and greedily, where everyone can see. They think they have found the weak one. It will take them a long time to look again at the one who said no.

events.text: A new pair of guards has been posted on your stair, and they know all the things you only told {npc}. You saw {him} this morning, and {he} was as warm as ever, and asked about your cough, and {he} has never had any idea that you had a cough until you told {him} yesterday, as a test, about a cough you do not have. Your cough is now mentioned in a report on the head's desk.

choices.text: Say nothing, and start telling {him} only what you want the head to hear

effects.log: You go on being warm too. You have a very bad cough this year, and a great many other things. {npc} is the most useful enemy you have ever had, until {he} works it out.

choices.text: Have it out with {him}, in {his} own rooms

effects.log: {npc} does not deny it. {He} pours you a cup of tea. "They have my son," {he} says. It is not an apology. It takes you a long time to get down the stairs.

mem.note: knows what I did

events.text: The head of {bh_the} has quoted something to you today, over the grain accounts, in passing. A small thing, a turn of phrase. You used it once, late at night, to {npc}, and to nobody else on this earth. The head of the house looks up from the page and gives you a very calm smile. You were meant to know.

choices.text: Smile back, and go on with the accounts

effects.log: You go through all the rest of the grain figures without a tremor. That night you go over what else you have told {npc}, one item at a time. It is a long list. You do not sleep.

choices.text: Offer {npc} twice what they are paying

ok.log: Everyone can be bought twice. {npc} looks almost relieved. From now on you will be told everything, and so will the head of the house, and {npc} will die rich, if {he} is careful.

fail.log: {npc} tells them about the offer the same night, of course. It is in fact the only honest thing {he} has done all year.

events.text: You arrive for the meeting at the old kiln, the one {npc} set up, the one that was going to bring in the east gate guard. It is a clear night. You can see the kiln from the ridge, and the path, and {npc} waiting there with a lantern. You can also see, because you came early and you came the long way, eleven people lying down in the bean field.

choices.text: Go home, and be in bed when they come to look

effects.log: You are in bed. You open the door to them in your sleeping robe, and you are so surprised. {npc} is looking at the floor, behind them. Neither of you will ever mention it.

choices.text: Go down there anyway, and put out the lantern

ok.log: The bean field does not go well for them. When it is over {npc} is still standing there, holding the dead lantern, with nothing at all to say to you. You take it out of {his} hand, and you walk home.

fail.log: You do not reach the kiln. It is a long and ugly way back to the ridge.

events.text: It costs you some months and more tea than you wish to remember, but you have the outline now. There is a path behind the back hall of {bh_the} that floods every spring, on purpose. Food goes up it once a year, a single bowl. Nobody will tell you who eats it, but a very old retainer, drunk, once called them {bh_anc}, and then begged you to forget. That name is on none of the tablets. It is not supposed to be on any tablet yet.

choices.text: Write the name down, and burn the paper

effects.log: You know it by heart now. You look up at that mountain differently. Anyone who beats the head of this house and thinks it is finished is going to have a very bad evening.

choices.text: Ask one more question: how long they have been up there

effects.log: The old retainer is sober by then, and he does not know you. But in the record of a long-ago flood, you find that bowl of rice being carried up. It is older than the family's oldest tablet. You stop asking.

events.text: You have been told, and you do not think you were meant to believe it. "The Old One is resting," says the small child who is showing you the persimmon tree, and she points with her whole arm at the back mountain of {bh_the}. Everybody here knows, it seems, the way that everybody knows where the well is. It is {bh_anc}. They were old when the child's great-grandfather was small. They do not come down. "Unless somebody is rude," she adds, and goes back to her persimmon.

choices.text: Thank her very gravely

effects.log: You thank her very gravely. You give her a sweet. You will think often about that word, rude, and about what the family would consider to be rude.

choices.text: Walk the foot of the mountain that evening

effects.log: You walk as far as the flood stones. Nothing happens. There is no one there and it is a beautiful evening. Every hair on your arms stands up, and it does not settle until you are back in your rooms.

events.text: You have spent a year on this. You have read the rice ledgers, walked the flooded path, and got the oldest retainer in {bh_the} drunk three separate times. There is a small house at the top of the back mountain, very clean, with one bowl. It belonged to someone. They died sixty years ago and the family has gone on carrying rice up there, because nobody could stand to be the one who stopped. Nobody is coming down.

choices.text: Leave the bowl where it is

effects.log: You leave it. You go down the path a little slower than you came up. Whatever you are planning, nothing up here is going to stop you. You find that you are not as pleased as you had expected.

choices.text: Eat the rice

effects.log: It is quite good rice. You wash the bowl, and you put it back. For the rest of your life, you will be the only person who knows that the ghost of {bh_the} has been fed for sixty years by someone with a sense of duty, and that it is gone.

events.text: It takes you four days to climb to the small house above {bh_the}. {bh_anc} is sitting on the step, shelling beans, and looks you over with the air of someone who has seen one of you before and was not impressed. "You will want to fight, or to beg," they say. "Everyone wants to fight or to beg. It has been so very dull. Can you do anything else?"

choices.text: Sit down, and shell beans, for as long as it takes

ok.log: You shell beans for nine days. On the tenth they ask you to tell them something they do not know. You tell them what the price of salt is now. They laugh until a bird falls out of the tree. "Come back," they say. "Bring news."

fail.log: You last three days. "Ah," they say, not looking up. "A fighter or a beggar after all." The path down is much steeper than the path up.

choices.text: Say you came to find out if they are real

effects.log: They hold up a bean. "As real as this." They crush it, and the whole mountain goes very slightly out of true, and comes back. "Now you know. Go home."

events.text: You have brought {bh_anc} the news: three years of it, written out. Which sect rose, who married whom, what they are wearing in the capital. They read it the way a starving person eats, and then they throw it down in disgust. "All this has happened before, in a different hat. Very well. Tell me something that has not. Tell me what you are actually doing in my grandchildren's house."

choices.text: Tell the truth

effects.log: You tell them all of it, the whole plan, on that step. They listen with their eyes closed. "It is not a very good plan," they say. "It is at least a new one. Come back when it is better."

choices.text: Tell them a lie so good it will amuse them

ok.log: It is a magnificent lie. It takes a whole afternoon. They applaud at the end. "I have not been lied to properly in two hundred years. You may come again. I know exactly what you are doing, by the way."

fail.log: They yawn at the second sentence. "No," they say. "Get off my step."

events.text: On your third climb {bh_anc} is waiting with a board laid out for stones and something in a jug. "You have bored me less than anyone since the dynasty before last," they say. "If you take that chair and rule it badly, I will come down and kill you, and I shall enjoy it very much. If you rule it interestingly, I may never have to get up. Your move." They have given you the weaker side, and they are smiling.

choices.text: Play, and do not let them win

ok.log: It takes all night. You lose by half a stone, and they are delighted. "You will do," says {bh_anc}. "I am going back to sleep. Do not wake me for anything smaller than the end of the world." You understand that a thing has been decided about you.

fail.log: You are beaten in forty moves. They look at the board with real sorrow. "Almost," they say. "Come back in ten years, if you are alive."

choices.text: Bow, and tell them the game is theirs

effects.log: You bow. "Yes," they say sadly, "it always is." They sweep the stones into the jug. You will never know what they were going to say next.

events.text: The small house above {bh_the} has a second cup set out on the table. It looks as though it has been set out for a long time. {bh_anc} sits with their back to you, looking at the valley, and does not turn. "If you are from the family," they say, in a voice that has gone a bit rusty, "then tell them I do not want the rice. If you are not, the water is at the back."

choices.text: Fetch the water, and wash the cup, and put it back

effects.log: You wash it. You put it back exactly where it was. They look at you then, for the first time. Their eyes are extremely old, and they do not say anything, and they do not send you away.

choices.text: Ask whose cup it is

ok.log: A very long silence. "His," they say. And then, after a while, they tell you. It was four hundred years ago, and the family has written it down wrongly, and they have been waiting all this time for someone to ask. You stay until dark.

fail.log: The silence goes on until you are quite sure you should not have said that. You find your own way down.

events.text: {bh_anc} has let you come back, and you have brought what they asked for: the family's official record of the death of the one whose cup that is. You have also brought the other record, the one you found in a tax file, that says what really happened, and who gave the order, and who signed it. It was the founder of this house. You have read it. You are holding it out now. They have not moved.

choices.text: Give them the real one

effects.log: They read it through once. Then they burn it in the stove, with care, and sit down. "I knew," says {bh_anc}. "But nobody has ever told me. Come back in spring."

choices.text: Give them the family's version, and keep the other

effects.log: They look at it and then at your other sleeve. "You are a very kind liar," they say. "It is not a thing I can use. Go home."

events.text: The last time you climb, it is snowing. {bh_anc} has cleared the path, which they have never done for anyone. "I have been keeping this family alive for four hundred years to spite one man," they say, "and he has been dead the whole time. I am tired, and I would like it to be someone else's problem. Do you intend to deserve that chair?" They are holding the second cup. It is full.

choices.text: Drink it, and say you will try

effects.log: It is only tea. It has been brewed very carefully. They watch you finish it. "That will do," says {bh_anc}. "I will not come down. Not for them, and not against you. Go on now." When you look back from the bend, the door is closed.

choices.text: Say that nobody deserves it, and that this is the whole trouble

ok.log: There is a pause, and then they begin to laugh, an awful rusty sound that goes on a long time and has tears in it. "That is what he said," they say. They pour the cup out in the snow, slowly. "Go on, then. I will not come down."

fail.log: They look at you as if they had expected something more. "Clever," they say. It is not praise. The second cup goes back on the table, still full.

events.text: There are no birds on this part of the back mountain of {bh_the}. There used to be a small house, and now there is a kind of hollow in the air where you find you do not want to walk. A voice comes up through the soles of your feet, patient and without any interest in you whatsoever. "Who is it that is still breathing so loudly?" It is {bh_anc}. You did not see anyone.

choices.text: Keep walking, and give your name

ok.log: It is the hardest hundred paces of your life. Your nose is bleeding by the end of them. You stand in the hollow and you say your name, and something very slowly takes an interest. "Again," it says. "Later. If there is any of you left."

fail.log: You stop at the sixtieth pace. You cannot make your foot go. You are found at the flood stones by a gardener, three days later, with no memory of coming down.

choices.text: Stop where you are, bow, and go back

effects.log: You bow in the direction of nothing, and you back all the way down. The birds begin again at the flood stones. You sit there for a while. It is a mark of wisdom, you tell yourself, and your hands agree.

events.text: You have climbed again into the place with no birds. This time {bh_anc} is visible, more or less: a very thin person, sitting absolutely still, with moss on one side. Their eyes are closed. They have been at the edge of something for several generations, and you have the clear feeling that you are standing inside their breath. "You will be asking me for something," they say, without moving anything to say it with. "It will have to be worth waking for."

choices.text: Offer to tell them why they should stay asleep

ok.log: You say that you are not worth waking for, and neither is anyone in the valley, and that they are very nearly there. The moss does not move. A long time later, you feel it: a very faint amusement, somewhere around the top of your skull. "Come once more."

fail.log: Halfway through your first sentence you find you have stopped talking, and you cannot start. It wears off by the bottom of the mountain.

choices.text: Sit down across from them, and breathe

effects.log: You sit, and you breathe, as slowly as you can. When you next notice anything, there is snow on your shoulders, and it was summer when you came up. You lost eight months. You have gained something too, and you are not sure what it is.

events.text: The third time, you bring nothing, and you say nothing. {bh_anc} opens one eye. You have never been looked at before. You had thought you had. Everything you have done in this life, and a certain amount from before it, is lifted out and looked at and set back very nearly where it was. "I see," it says. "Small. But it is going somewhere. I will not get up for that. Do not make me regret having looked."

choices.text: Hold still under it

ok.log: You hold still. When the eye closes, you find you have been standing on your own feet the whole time, which surprises you. Nothing will come down from here to stop you. You are not sure you have been given anything except that.
